name: Massachusetts
modelName: Income shares by formula: weekly combined available income x marginal percentages by income band (Table A), adjusted for number (Table B) and ages (Table C) of children
incomeLabel: Gross income before taxes, as the state guideline defines it.

tableA.note: $15 per week unless the court deviates

statute.name: G.L. c. 208, § 28; c. 209C, § 9; Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines (Trial Court, effective December 1, 2025)

incomeDefinition: Gross income from all sources listed in Guidelines Section I.A (wages, self-employment, Social Security retirement/disability, dividends, etc., with a catch-all for any other compensation, I.A.30), excluding means-tested benefits. Available income (worksheet line 2/3a) = gross weekly income + Social Security dependency benefit sent to the parent - other support obligations paid - health care premium/enrollment and dental/vision insurance actually paid, not less than $0 (2025 Guidelines § II.H-I; CJD 304 lines 2-3).
modelText: All amounts weekly, rounded to the nearest dollar. (1) Each parent's available income; combined available income (3b) and each parent's share (3c). (2) Applicable income 3d = combined income capped at $8,654 a week ($450,000 a year). (3) Support for one child 3e from Table A on 3d (the first two bands use the payor's own gross income). (4) Multiply by the Table B factor for the number of children (3g). (5) Reduce by the Table C percentage for children aged 18 or older (4a-4c). (6) Each parent's share = 3c x 4c; add the other parent's share of child care costs up to $430 per week per child (line 6). (7) Box 2 (children with one parent about 2/3 of the time): if the payor's support is under 10% of the recipient's available income, it is limited to the lesser of 6e, 6g, or (7a + 10%) x payor income, but not below the chart's shaded minimum (line 7b). Box 1 (shared approximately equally) and Box 3 (split): the worksheet computes each parent's share and the parent with the larger amount pays the difference. (8) Subtract Social Security dependency benefits sent to the recipient for the payor's retirement/disability (7c-7d). Orders of 40% or more of the payor's available income are presumptively a substantial hardship (7e). Income above $8,654 a week: discretionary, at a percentage below 10% (line 8; § II.C.2).
sharedText: Worksheet line 1b has three boxes: Box 1 shared approximately equally, Box 2 primary residence with one parent about 2/3 of the time, Box 3 split (each parent has at least one child). The guidelines assume about one-third parenting time for the non-residential parent; substantially less or more (but under one-half) is a ground for deviation (2025 Guidelines § II.D.1-4). There is no overnight threshold.
addOnsText: other parent's share of child care costs, up to $430 per child per week, added to the payor's support (worksheet line 6) premiums actually paid are deducted from the paying parent's gross income (not added to support) Reasonable out-of-pocket child care costs actually paid, up to $430 per week per child, are shared in proportion to available income (§ II.E.1). Health care and dental/vision premiums are deducted from the payer parent's gross income (§ II.H.1, II.I.1). Health care coverage is reasonable in cost if it does not exceed 5% of the parent's gross income (§ II.H).
lowIncomeText: Payor gross income of $301 a week or less: order of no more than $15 a week; $302 to $391: no more than $33 a week (Table A: $15 + 20% above $301). The court may deviate higher or lower, including to $0 (§ II.C.1). The 2025 Task Force set $301 and $391 at 100% and 130% of the 2025 poverty guideline for one person and calls $391 a week the minimum subsistence level (Commentary 2025, § II.C).

emancipation.text: The court may, but need not, order support for a child aged 18 to 21 who lives with and is principally dependent on a parent, and to 23 if enrolled in an undergraduate program; the guidelines reduce support for such children through Table C, and a child aged 18+ still in high school is treated as under 18 (2025 Guidelines § II.F; G.L. c. 208, § 28).

facts.text: The 2025 Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines took effect December 1, 2025 (signed by the Chief Justice of the Trial Court on October 30, 2025) and supersede all previous guidelines (Preamble).
The guidelines apply up to $450,000 of combined annual available income ($8,654 a week), raised from $400,000 in 2021; above that, support on the excess is discretionary at less than 10% (§ II.C.2).
Child care costs are shared only up to a benchmark of $430 per week per child, based on the average cost of center-based infant care in Massachusetts (§ II.E.1 and 2025 Commentary).

Support can be ordered for children up to age 23, but is reduced (Table C, e.g. 25% when all children are 18 or older) and contribution to college costs is generally capped at 50% of UMass Amherst in-state costs (§ II.F-G).
A child support order of 40% or more of the payor's available income creates a rebuttable presumption of substantial hardship justifying a deviation (worksheet line 7e; § IV).

sources.name: Massachusetts: G.L. c. 208, § 28; c. 209C, § 9; Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines (Trial Court, effective December 1, 2025)

testCases.source: Computed by hand with CJD 304: combined $2,000 -> Table A $346 + 18% x $400 = $418 (the 2025 Guidelines Chart gives the same one-child amounts for every income from $392 to $8,654: all 1,105 chart entries match Table A, see scripts/cs_massachusetts.py); x Table B 1.00; payor share 75% = 313.50 -> $314; line 7a 314/500 = 62.8% >= 10%, so no disparity limit.
